question: Can we estimate the population distribution of latent class-average treatment effects from treatment, outcomes, and two proxies, uniformly even when effects coincide? The existing approach recovers effects and class masses through eigenvalues and individual eigenvectors. Its simultaneous recovery guarantees require separated effects: eigenvectors become unstable near collisions, and equal effects cannot distinguish their classes through the effect matrix. The proposed target combines population masses at equal effect values.
result: The target is ν_P = Σ_u p_u δ_{τ_u}, with p_u = P(U=u) and τ_u = E[Y(1)|U=u] − E[Y(0)|U=u]. The model requires consistency and Y(t) ⟂ T | U; Z ⟂ (X,Y) | (T,U); X ⟂ (Y,T) | U; and X_1=1. Dimensions and supplied constants are fixed and known, with 2≤k≤min{d_x,d_z}; P(U=u,T=t)≥π_0; the smallest singular values of A_0,A_1,B are at least σ_0; and ||X||_2, ||ZXᵀ||_op, ||YZXᵀ||_op are bounded by L. Under these conditions, for every P,Q∈M, W_1(ν_P,ν_Q)≤C_mod d_S(S(P),S(Q)), where S contains the two proxy cross-moments, two outcome-weighted cross-moments, and population proxy mean. Thus these observable moments identify the law and control its error linearly. Two constructed estimators satisfy, for every P∈M, n≥1, and 0<η<1/2, P_O^{⊗n}{max[W_1(λ̂_n,ν_P),W_1(ν̂_n,ν_P)] > C√[log(C/η)/n]}≤η. Constants depend only on dimensions, bounds, and overlap and proxy-rank margins; no effect-separation condition enters.
mechanism: 1. Form M_t=E[ZXᵀ|T=t], N_t=E[YZXᵀ|T=t], and m_X=E[X]. Proxy separation factors M_t as A_t diag(q_t)Bᵀ, where q_t contains within-arm class shares; N_t inserts the class outcome means into that factorization. 2. Choose an orthonormal basis V for the common signal row space. In ΔQ=(M_1V)†N_1V−(M_0V)†N_0V, inversion cancels reference-proxy features and arm shares. With R=BᵀV, ΔQ=R^{-1}diag(τ)R. Its eigenvalues therefore locate effects. 3. Recover population weighting through aᵀ=m_XᵀV=pᵀR and c=Vᵀe_1=R^{-1}1. Consequently aᵀf(ΔQ)c=Σ_u p_u f(τ_u), including when effects repeat. 4. Compare these integrals over all one-Lipschitz functions to control Wasserstein distance, using the gap-cancellation argument. 5. For the first estimator, project the empirical summary onto the closure of feasible population summaries and apply the extended identified law map. Because the true summary is feasible, projection increases summary error by at most a factor of two. 6. For the grid estimator, construct a thresholded empirical effect operator in the original proxy coordinates. Search conditioned factors (V,R,p,τ), fitting their implied operator, population proxy mean, and constant-coordinate normalization. Return the selected candidate's probability law. A rounded version of the true factors has approximation error of order n^{-1/2}; the minimizer fits at least as well, and the three residuals control law error. Uniform concentration of the empirical summaries then yields both estimation guarantees.
why_true: The unstable object is the individual eigenvector decomposition, whereas the target only needs population-weighted integrals of functions of effects. For two effect operators, let H=RR'^{-1}. The identity (τ_i−τ'_j)H_ij=[R(Δ−Δ')R'^{-1}]_ij connects coordinate mixing to operator error. Replacing the effect difference by f(τ_i)−f(τ'_j) cannot increase its magnitude when f is one-Lipschitz. Fixed dimensions and conditioned proxy coordinates control conversion to operator norms without dividing by an effect gap. The anchors supply population weights, and their transformations cancel the spectral coordinates. Intuitively, assigning mass to separate nearby effects can have uncertainty proportional to error divided by their distance, but transporting that uncertain mass multiplies by the same distance. The projection and grid constructions preserve valid probability laws, while bounded contributions and overlap make observable-summary error uniformly of order n^{-1/2}.
example: The two-class population has masses 0.4 and 0.6, untreated means both 0.25, and treated means 0.5−ε and 0.5+ε. Hence ν_P=0.4δ_{0.25−ε}+0.6δ_{0.25+ε}, for 0≤ε≤1/8. Moving both masses to 0.25 costs ε. The displayed proxy mean matrices remain fixed and informative throughout this collision, with L=2 and π_0=σ_0=0.1. At ε=0, ΔQ=0.25I_2 and the anchors recover total mass one without choosing individual eigenvectors. Moving mass h between the two effects costs 2ε|h|, illustrating why uncertain separate masses need not destabilize the law.

findings.problem: The further results introduce 'our calibrated two-class model' and 'ordered masses' without precisely specifying the minimax parameter domain or the ordering. Both sharp-rate results are stated only in words, so I cannot reproduce their precise risk statements.
findings.fix: Specify the calibrated parameter class and say whether masses are ordered by increasing effect. Show the corresponding infimum-over-estimators, supremum-over-populations expected-risk formulas, with rates n^{-1/2} and min{1,1/(√n g)}.
